# What is GIS, and why use QGIS? - Statistics Canada QGIS Demo 1

> **Provenance note:** This file comes from the publisher's web page, not from Brightspace. Verbatim retrieval was not possible through the available fetch tool (it returned a detailed paraphrase only), so the text below is a faithful point-by-point **paraphrase of the published transcript**, with UI names quoted as they appear in the transcript. It is not an auto-caption and not verbatim.

Presenter: Alex Foster, data analyst, Statistics Canada. First video of the QGIS Demo series, aimed at new GIS users.

1. Introduces Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and their relevance to many work areas. Two parts: what GIS and spatial data are; why the series uses QGIS (open source).
2. The series starts from foundations and builds to advanced topics; skills transfer to the viewer's own datasets.
3. GIS programs store, process, combine and visualize spatial data - any dataset with coordinate information that positions it.
4. Everyday examples: map/GPS route-finding, storm weather maps.
5. GIS supports linking, analysis and visualization; overlaying datasets as interactive multi-scale maps informs decisions in social, economic, business, service, environmental and land-use matters.
6. Ranges from simple mapping to scripting and modelling; most beginner uses need only a few steps.
7. Maps make multidisciplinary information easier to understand; combining datasets can produce new information.
8. Examples shown: a heat map of 2017 traffic collision frequency in Ottawa; a time series of 2016 mean monthly temperatures across Manitoba.
9. QGIS: free, open source, graphical-interface focused; integrates SAGA and GRASS toolsets; supports user plugins; small install and low computing requirements; large community, frequent updates, online documentation.
10. Download: link in video description or search online. Windows options: the **OSGEO4W Package** (advanced users; automates updates, avoids duplicate shared packages) or **stand-alone Installers**.
11. Stand-alone versions at recording: **v. 3.6** "The Most Recent Feature Rich Release" and **v. 3.4**, the long-term release first published February 2019. Presenter picks 3.4 (stable LTR). Other OSes: installers in the download page drop-downs.
12. Install with defaults (Next until Finish). Open **QGIS Desktop** from the Start bar or desktop shortcut; in the pop-up choose **"Fresh Start"** (not importing QGIS 2 settings).
13. Repeat download steps to update.
14. Next video: categories and file formats of spatial data and downloading from **Open Maps** (federal spatial data archive).

Course note: the course recommends the current QGIS Long Term Release rather than 3.4 ([Getting Started](../../course-pages/getting-started-with-course-software.md)).
